Series::igammac¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series Series::igammac(const Series& other) const
Series Series::igammac(double other) const
Series& Series::igammac_(const Series& other) const

What It Does¶

Computes the regularized upper incomplete gamma function Q(a, x) elementwise — the complement of igamma. self is the shape parameter a, the argument is the lower limit x:

Q(a, x) = ( 1 / Gamma(a) ) * integral_x^inf t^(a-1) e^(-t) dt = 1 - P(a, x)

Q(a, .) is the survival function of a Gamma(a, rate 1) variable, so igammac gives right-tail probabilities directly: the chi-square survival function with k degrees of freedom is Q(k/2, x/2), which is what a goodness-of-fit p-value needs.

The reason to call igammac rather than 1 - igamma(x): when the upper tail is small, P(a, x) is close to 1 and 1 - P cancels most of its significant digits. Q is computed on its own footing and stays accurate deep into the tail — note the 4.3e-08 in Example 1, a value 1 - igamma could not resolve.

Behaviour:

  • Q(a, 0) = 1 and Q(a, x) -> 0 as x -> inf; monotone decreasing in x.

  • P(a, x) + Q(a, x) = 1.

  • Defined for a > 0 and x >= 0; NaN outside.

Parameters¶

other (const Series& or double): the lower limit x, broadcast against self.

Returns¶

Series A Series broadcast over a and x, each element Q(a, x) in [0, 1].

Gradient¶

igammac is differentiable with respect to x (the other argument, when it is a Series). It is the negative of the igamma derivative, since Q = 1 - P:

d/dx Q(a, x) = -x^(a-1) e^(-x) / Gamma(a)

There is no gradient with respect to a. As with igamma, an objective that reaches its input only through the shape parameter — or through the igammac(double) overload, which holds x constant — is disconnected, and reverse() on it raises.

In-Place Form¶

igammac_() is the in-place sibling of igammac(): it computes the same result and writes it back into self directly — mutating it (and any other handle sharing the same storage) instead of allocating a new Series — then returns a reference to self.

Despite being declared const at the call site — a quirk of how this method’s wrapper is generated, not a promise that self is left unchanged — igammac_() genuinely mutates the series it’s called on.

auto x = pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0});
auto y = pluss::make_series({1.0, 1.0});

x.igammac_(y);
std::cout << x;

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[2], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[0.36787944, 0.73575888]

Examples¶

Example 1. With a = 2 fixed, Q falls from 1 toward 0 as x grows, and stays accurate in the far tail.

std::cout << pluss::make_series({2.0, 2.0, 2.0, 2.0})
                 .igammac(pluss::make_series({0.0, 1.0, 3.0, 20.0}));

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[4], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[1, 0.73575888, 0.19914827, 4.3284226e-08]

Example 2. At a = 1 the upper tail is the exponential survival function, Q(1, x) = e^(-x).

auto x = pluss::make_series({0.5, 1.0, 2.0});
pluss::series::print(std::cout, pluss::make_series({1.0, 1.0, 1.0}).igammac(x));
pluss::series::print(std::cout, x.neg().exp());

Output¶

Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[0.6065, 0.3679, 0.1353]
Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[0.6065, 0.3679, 0.1353]

Example 3. The backward pass with respect to x is the Gamma density negated.

auto x = pluss::make_series({1.0, 3.0});
x.tracks_slope_(true);
pluss::make_series({2.0, 2.0}).igammac(x).sum().reverse();

pluss::series::print(std::cout, x.sensitivity());

Output¶

Series(shape=[2], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[-0.3679, -0.1494]

Same magnitudes as the igamma example, opposite sign.

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • Argument order is a.igammac(x): self is the shape parameter.

  • Prefer igammac(x) to 1 - igamma(x) for small tails — the subtraction loses precision exactly where you need it.

  • Gradient flows only through x, and only when x is a Series. No gradient with respect to a; a shape-only objective is disconnected and reverse() raises.

  • a <= 0 or x < 0 gives NaN.

Summary¶

igammac(x) is the regularized upper incomplete gamma Q(a, x) = 1 - P(a, x), with a from self:

  • the survival function of a Gamma(a, 1); chi-square survival is Q(k/2, x/2)

  • falls from 1 to 0 in x; accurate in the far tail where 1 - igamma is not

  • NaN for a <= 0 or x < 0

  • differentiable in x with backward -x^(a-1) e^(-x) / Gamma(a); not in a

  • Series::igamma: the lower tail P(a, x).

  • Series::lgamma: the Gamma(a) normalizer.

  • Series::erfc: the complementary error function, the analogous “compute the small tail directly” routine for the Gaussian.
